languages._comment_docker_repo: Official docker.io/library/rust images. Old minors <=1.54 are Debian stretch/buster-based (buster confirmed through 1.54, bullseye confirmed starting exactly at 1.55 -- verified live via `docker run rust:X.Y-slim cat /etc/os-release` across the whole transition window, not estimated) and need the same archive.debian.org mirror fix already used elsewhere in this project for EOL Debian codenames.

versions.notes: 1.0-1.30 predate this project's confirmed Docker image floor (rust:1.31-slim, 2018-12-06, is the oldest pullable official tag -- verified live via `docker manifest inspect`). No image ever existed for these historically real compiler versions in this registry.

Reinstated 2026-07-25: originally excluded after hitting a syn/serde_derive/proc-macro2/quote resolution wall that appeared specific to very old rustc -- confirmed via direct testing at rustc 1.36 that this was actually a GENERAL ecosystem MSRV/manifest-syntax drift problem (crates.io's live serde/serde_derive/serde_json/quote/proc-macro2/tinyvec releases keep climbing past what old rustc can parse), now fixed generally in lang_rust.py via explicit version caps on those specific crates, not something unique to 1.31.

Excluded from this registry's sparse language-version coverage (rebuilt 2026-07-24, by explicit user decision): no framework or cryptography-library bucket in this registry has a compatibility floor at this exact minor, and it is not a Rust edition or Debian codename transition point. Every (framework, library) pairing already has a working rust_ver among the included set -- for any pair, the required combined floor is max(fw_floor, lib_floor), which is always one of the two floors themselves, both already covered. Unlike framework/library include/exclude (editable via the dashboard's version_overrides table), language versions are NOT dashboard-editable by deliberate design -- if a future addition needs this exact version, it must be included here manually.

version.notes: Floor corrected 2026-07-30 (was an era-based 1.31-1.38 estimate): warp 0.1.23's own real, unpinned transitive dependency graph (fetched fresh from crates.io, same lockgen-vs-builder-stage gap this whole project's msrv_repair mechanism exists for) hits a genuinely long tail of DIFFERENT undeclared-floor crates in rapid succession as rustc climbs from 1.36 to 1.45 -- hashbrown-via-indexmap (ptr.cast, ~1.38), lazy_static (cfg(doctest), ~1.40), urlencoding (matches! macro, 1.42), zeroize (isize::MAX associated const, ~1.43), opaque-debug (resolver-feature manifest field cargo can't parse, needs ~1.51+) -- each individually cappable in principle, but confirmed live via direct isolated bisection (matching this registry's own real-build-verification standard) that rustc 1.54 is the first sparse-set value where the ENTIRE dependency graph compiles cleanly end-to-end. Same class of correction as Iron's own 1.31->1.55 fix and rsa 0.8's 1.56->1.60 fix -- accepting a real, build-confirmed floor rather than exhaustively chasing every transitive crate's own undeclared MSRV one at a time. 1.69-1.74 REMOVED 2026-07-31 (a real user batch run surfaced this, not this session's own earlier verification): at rustc >=1.69, warp 0.1 (via its own idna/url chain) reaches the SAME icu4x hub as axum/warp 0.3+, and hits the EXACT same `yoke 0.7.5` MSRV wall (needs rustc 1.71.1) already found and fixed for axum 0.6/0.7 in this registry -- confirmed via `cargo tree -i yoke` that icu_collections/icu_provider/zerovec (real, published crates.io releases, not something this project controls) hard-require yoke>=0.7.5 directly, so no ecosystem_caps range on our own side can route around it; axum 0.6/0.7 hit the identical wall and were corrected the same way (skip 1.69-1.74 entirely, resume coverage at 1.75 where yoke's own floor is finally satisfied) rather than continuing to chase this narrow, recurring icu4x/zerovec/yoke boundary.

Floor corrected 2026-07-30 (was an era-based 1.39-1.44 estimate, same class of correction as warp 0.1's own 1.31->1.54 fix): confirmed live via real build that `futures-util` has almost its ENTIRE 0.3.0-0.3.30 release range YANKED from crates.io (verified directly via the crates.io versions API) -- only 0.3.31+ remains, and 0.3.31 itself declares rust_version=1.56. This is a genuine, permanent impossibility (no older non-yanked futures-util exists at all to fall back to), not a bug to route around -- same class as the bcrypt-0.5/blowfish yanked-version impossibility found earlier in this registry. Confirmed via a clean real build at rustc 1.56. 1.69-1.74 REMOVED 2026-07-31 (a real user batch run surfaced this): exactly the same pattern already found and fixed for warp 0.1 -- 11 different libraries (bcrypt/ring/argon2/rsa/openssl/sodiumoxide/rust-crypto) all hit the identical `yoke 0.7.5` MSRV wall (needs rustc 1.71.1) at exactly 1.69/1.70, and warp 0.2 has NO icu4x-hub protection at all (explicitly excluded from that scoping in lang_rust.py, since applying it unconditionally previously broke its own otherwise-working resolution). FURTHER NARROWED the same day once a SEPARATE library (ed25519-dalek bucket "1") turned out to reach the SAME wall even earlier, at rustc 1.61 specifically (confirmed live: 1.60 builds cleanly, 1.61 does not) -- library-dependent reachability, not a single uniform threshold across the whole framework bucket. Rather than chase a separate narrow exception per library, extended the removed window down to 1.61-1.74 (was just 1.69-1.74), leaving only 1.56-1.60 as warp 0.2's confirmed-safe lower range, matching the same established fix as axum 0.6/0.7 and warp 0.1: skip the whole unsafe window, resume coverage at 1.75 where the wall's own floor is finally satisfied for every library tested so far.

Floor corrected 2026-07-30 (was an era-based 1.45-1.74 estimate): warp 0.3 reaches the exact same icu4x-hub `yoke` MSRV wall (needs rustc 1.71.1) already found and fixed for axum 0.6/0.7 -- confirmed live via a real build failure at rustc 1.70 (one minor below the wall) that even with the icu4x-hub caps correctly scoped to warp too, the WIDER icu4x resolution at that narrow boundary surfaces a further pre-1.0/1.x icu_properties-vs-icu_provider instance-routing conflict (`gen_any_buffer_constructors` macro missing, a genuinely different icu4x API era mismatch). Confirmed clean at rustc 1.75 in ~40s (vs 1600+ seconds and a long tail of unrelated genuine floors at 1.45). Same pragmatic choice already made for axum 0.6/0.7 in this registry: accept the real, build-confirmed 1.75 floor rather than continue chasing the narrow 1.69-1.74 boundary of this same recurring icu4x/zerovec/yoke family.

version.notes: MSRV 1.41, confirmed via GitHub issue discussion. Resolves to latest 1.x.

Corrected 2026-07-26 from the originally-cited GitHub issue #194 MSRV (1.60.0) after real builds surfaced two more layers: (1) our own Cargo.toml was missing ed25519-dalek's own "rand_core" feature, without which SigningKey::generate() (used by our touch code) doesn't even exist -- confirmed via source (signing.rs: `#[cfg(feature = "rand_core")]`), not an MSRV issue at all, now fixed in lang_rust.py; (2) even with that fixed, the resolved der/pkcs8/spki chain (pulled in via the `ed25519` crate's optional pkcs8 feature-unification) uniformly requires rustc 1.65 with no same-class candidate below it. 1.65 confirmed via a real build + run (curl-verified touch output) after both fixes; 1.60-1.64 do NOT work despite issue #194's claim. Genuine breaking API rewrite (signing-context/verify changes) from 1.x still applies as the reason this is a distinct bucket from "1".

Corrected 2026-08-01: this bucket resolves to ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 (2026-07-06), which ships edition="2024" and rust-version="1.85" (confirmed via a real GitHub source diff, dalek-cryptography/curve25519-dalek tags ed25519-2.2.0...ed25519-3.0.0 -- this crate now lives in that monorepo, not its own repo). The compatibility range inherited via the dashboard Include action (1.65-1.97, from bucket "2") was wrong the same way bcrypt 0.18/0.19 were -- narrowed to 1.85+. Separately, 3.0.0 is also a real API break, not just an MSRV bump: SigningKey::generate() changed its RNG trait bound from rand_core 0.6s CryptoRngCore to rand_core 0.10s CryptoRng, and the crates own doc examples replaced rand::rngs::OsRng with getrandom::SysRng wrapped in UnwrapErr -- see _ED25519_DALEK_3_IMPORTS/_TOUCH in lang_rust.py.

version.notes: Resolves to 0.2.36, the FINAL release -- confirmed genuinely abandoned (zero commits since 2016), RUSTSEC-2016-0005 unmaintained. The crate's OWN README carries a warning: "has not been thoroughly audited for correctness, so any use where security is important is not recommended." Compatibility is the full range as an OPTIMISTIC estimate -- whether 2016-era pure-Rust code still compiles unmodified on rustc 1.97 has NOT been verified with a real build and may well fail (language/edition changes over a decade are a real risk); treat this as the single most likely combo in the whole registry to need a real-build fix.
